concept.name: Donchian Channel
concept.definition: Richard Donchian's price channel plotting the highest high and lowest low of the last n periods (commonly 20) as upper and lower bands, with an optional midline at their average; the basis of classic breakout systems such as the Turtle Traders' rules.
concept.intuition: The channel shows the extremes of the recent trading range; a close outside it is by definition a new n-period high or low, which breakout traders treat as trend initiation.
concept.mechanics: Upper = max(High, n); Lower = min(Low, n); Middle = (Upper + Lower)/2. Breakouts beyond the bands generate trend-following signals, and the channel width reads volatility; the bands also serve as trailing stop and support/resistance references.
concept.formula: UC = max(High, N); LC = min(Low, N); Middle = (UC + LC)/2, typically N = 20.
concept.failure_modes: False breakouts are common in sideways markets where price repeatedly pokes the bands; as a purely lagging construction it gives no warning before the breakout occurs.
concept.misconceptions: Touching the upper band is not 'overbought' - it is a new n-period high, the exact condition trend-followers buy; the channel records extremes, it does not predict them.
concept.example: 20-day high 105, low 95: upper band 105, lower 95, midline 100; a close at 106 is an upside breakout.
